verdict_valid_for: reviewed_sha256 only; any re-review must cite the new hash
method: read the artifact from disk in full, hashed before and after; checked (a) class leakage, (b) conclusion inflation, (c) assumption completeness, (d) decidability of the falsifier, (e) fields two competent readers could read non-equivalently. One citation spot-check performed independently (arXiv:1912.08478 abstract, fetched 2026-09-11).
score_scale: 0-5, one reviewer's dimensional judgement; not a universal score and not an aggregate
score_rationale: Strong structure: explicit class decomposition, transfer-failure table, regularity separation, provenance disclaimers, and no class leakage or conclusion inflation. Not acceptable yet: the operative statement asserts an equivalence the artifact itself marks unverified; the falsifier tier is stronger than the formal statement; the non-vacuity condition imports unnecessary black-hole content; and the artifact changed three times under one revision label during the review, so no hash-stable revision existed to accept.
hard_failure_note: No HF in the current taxonomy (HF-01..HF-13) is triggered by the reviewed revision. The findings below are acceptance blockers that the taxonomy does not yet name; recommend adding a schema-internal-consistency HF (dangling refs, self-contradictory status) and a revision-label-stability HF.

findings.statement: The operative fields assert an equivalence the artifact itself marks unverified. i_plus.completeness_definition says '... complete to the future; equivalently every future-directed causal curve reaching I+ is complete to the past' (l.247) while equivalent_forms.equivalence_status is 'unverified' (l.255). conclusion.statement repeats 'equivalently, every future-directed causal curve that reaches I+ is complete to the past' (l.278-279) while equivalence_claim.status is 'unverified' (l.284).
findings.why_it_matters: Geodesic-generator completeness of I+ and past-completeness of every causal curve reaching I+ are not equivalent in general. As written, two readers can evaluate the same spacetime differently against the schema's own statement, and a verdict cannot be tied to one truth condition.
findings.required_change: Remove the 'equivalently' clause from conclusio.statement and i_plus.completeness_definition, or promote the equivalence out of the statement into a clearly tagged unverified variant. Do not mark the schema pinned while an unverified equivalence is load-bearing inside the statement.

findings.evidence_lines_reviewed_revision: header revision history (l.14-26), map artifact_sha256, observed disk hashes
findings.statement: The dispatched target (f15ea52380d2, r2), the map-pinned artifact hash (f55722a7...), and the on-disk bytes changed during the review: f15ea52380d2 -> f55722a7... -> a7ef0398dfb7 -> 7a3e1f93f77c, while the header kept revision: 3 and revised_at unchanged. The F1 canonical was declared FROZEN at f15ea523 by the controller status of 23:26:04.
findings.why_it_matters: A review verdict can only bind a hash. In-place edits under a fixed revision label defeat both the map's artifact_sha256 and the A1 independence check; the artifact_hash map now disagrees with the file on disk.
findings.required_change: Stop editing schemas/af_wcc_vacuum.yaml; declare one frozen sha256 (bump the revision label and revised_at on any future change); re-dispatch reviews against that hash; have Astra re-pin artifact_sha256 or mark the drift as a hard audit failure.

findings.statement: non_vacuity.condition requires 'at least one data set in D_gen whose maximal development is future-incomplete with a non-empty black-hole region'. This merges three different requirements: (i) D_gen non-empty (needed for the universal not to be vacuous), (ii) existence of a D_gen datum with a future-incomplete development (needed for the hiding clause to have content), and (iii) a non-empty black-hole region, which the WCC statement does not require.
findings.why_it_matters: A naked singularity without a horizon would still make the hiding question non-trivial; requiring a black-hole region biases the class toward one formation scenario and is not implied by the statement. It is the kind of smuggled physical assumption the audit rubric (HF-06) exists to catch, even though it sits in a witness field rather than in the statement.
findings.required_change: Split the condition: (i) D_gen non-empty; (ii) at least one D_gen datum with future-incomplete development; move black-hole formation to a separate optional physical-scenario field. Keep witness_status unresolved.

findings.statement: falsifier.tier_1 demands 'an open set ... of data in D_gen' (robustness: 'open (or at least residual) set ... not on a single fine-tuned member') to refute the class. The formal statement (l.126) is a universal over D_GEN; a single member of D_gen with a visible boundary point makes it false.
findings.why_it_matters: The tier-1 falsifier is strictly stronger than the statement, so a valid logical refutation can be classified as not-a-refutation. That inverts the project rule that a falsifier is the cheapest decisive test.
findings.required_change: Separate logical refutation (one witness datum in D_gen) from acceptance robustness (an open/residual family). Label the latter tier_1-robust and keep it distinct from tier_1.

findings.statement: falsifier.machine_checkable_steps lists 'check membership in D_gen, in particular the genericity clause' and 'verify that the maximal development is future-incomplete' as machine-checkable. Membership in a residual set defined as an intersection of open dense sets is not decidable from a finite datum description, and future-incompleteness of a development is a proof obligation, not a finite computation.
findings.why_it_matters: Overstating decidability inflates what a verifier can accept; the project's entry criterion is that a machine, not a reader, decides.
findings.required_change: Split the list into machine_checkable (constraint equations; explicit incomplete geodesic witness with a checkable incompleteness proof) and proof_obligations (D_gen membership; maximality/future-incompleteness), each with the evidence type that would discharge it.

findings.statement: quantifier_order_status and acceptance_map.exact_quantifiers are 'pinned' while D_GEN's definition depends on genericity.generic_set (proposed_pending_A1, l.232) and the weighted norm (s,delta) is proposed_by_F1_unreviewed (l.188-196).
findings.why_it_matters: The quantifier prefix is pinned; the quantifier domains are not. A reader can mistake 'exact quantifiers: pinned' for 'the formal statement is fixed'.
findings.required_change: Mark exact_quantifiers as 'prefix pinned; domains pending genericity/weight review', or split prefix from domains.

findings.statement: The self-check records that the flash-04 ambiguity runner was run on revision 2 and that 're-run expected before any gate claim' for revision 3.
findings.why_it_matters: The artifact itself declares the r3 ambiguity evidence incomplete; this is consistent with the revise verdict and must be discharged before G-FORM.
findings.required_change: Run the ambiguity runner on the frozen revision and attach the report hash; record F1-AMB-15 disposition.

findings.statement: In the reviewed revision, data_class.unresolved_refs and acceptance_map referenced unresolved[data_class.mass], unresolved[data_class.topology] and unresolved[visibility.curve_class], none of which existed in the unresolved list. In the later in-place bytes observed at 7a3e1f93 the references are gone (data_class.unresolved_refs now lists only weighted_norm; topology/visibility unresolved_ref are null).
findings.why_it_matters: Dangling references break the 'every unresolved field is listed' stop rule. Fixed by silent edit rather than by a revision bump, which is itself covered by F1-16-02.
findings.required_change: If visibility.curve_class and data_class.mass are still open decisions, restore them as unresolved entries rather than deleting the references; if they are decided, record the decision in-line as done for slice_topology.
